title: Ubiquiti
desc: UniFi networking, cameras, door access and ISP wireless

pages.t: Ubiquiti (now Ubiquiti Inc.) was founded in 2003 by Robert Pera and is listed on the New York Stock Exchange. It started with wireless radios and grew into a broad range of networking products for homes and businesses.

UniFi is the best-known line. It targets home, prosumer and business customers with network gear, IP cameras, door access and phones. Other lines such as airMAX, airFiber and UFiber serve internet providers and are managed in UISP.
g: A buyer between home user and professional: wants business-grade gear but often sets it up themselves.
A security camera that sends video over the network instead of a special video cable.

pages.t: The ui.com home page pitches unified networking, physical security and more, under the tagline "License Free". For a distributor, that means one vendor can cover the network, cameras and door control for the same customer.

quiz.q: Which Ubiquiti line is the best known and targets home, prosumer and business customers?
quiz.w: UniFi is the company's best-known line. EdgeMax is an older wired routing and switching line, and UFiber is the fibre line for internet providers.

quiz.q: What does Ubiquiti's own site describe as its idea?
o: Only cheap Wi-Fi routers for consumers
Networking, physical security and more, unified
quiz.w: The home page presents networking, physical security and more as one unified offering.

quiz.q: Which term describes a buyer who wants business-grade gear but often sets it up themselves?
quiz.w: Prosumer sits between home user and professional.
g: A buyer between home user and professional.

pages.t: UniFi hardware is managed from a console, a box that runs UniFi OS. Many gateways such as the Dream Machine and Cloud Gateway are consoles. You add apps to it, and each app handles one area.
g: The UniFi box (often a gateway) that runs the management software for the whole site.
The device that connects your local network to the internet and enforces rules.

pages.t: Typical apps: Network (gateway, switches, Wi-Fi), Protect (cameras), Access (doors), Talk (phones) and Connect (signage and EV charging). One login and one look and feel across them.

New UniFi devices are adopted into the console, then configured centrally, locally or remotely through a web portal and the mobile apps. That is why installers like it: one place to see the whole site.
g: UniFi term for connecting a new device to your console so it can be managed centrally.

quiz.q: What runs the UniFi apps for a site?
quiz.w: A console running UniFi OS hosts the apps such as Network and Protect.

quiz.q: Which app manages the cameras?
quiz.w: Protect is the camera app. Access is doors and Talk is phones.

quiz.q: What does 'adopt' mean in UniFi?
o: Connecting a new device to the console to manage it
quiz.w: Adopting links the device to the console so it is configured centrally.
g: Connect a device to your console so it can be managed.

pages.t: A gateway connects the site to the internet. UniFi gateways add a firewall, intrusion prevention, VPN and support for more than one internet line. Many models double as the console that runs the apps.
g: Virtual Private Network: a secure tunnel between sites or to a remote user.
Software or hardware that filters traffic between networks.

pages.t: Ubiquiti positions Cloud Gateway Ultra and Max for small-to-medium sites, Dream Machine Pro and Pro Max for large-scale sites, and Enterprise Firewall models for the most demanding networks. Dream Router 7 adds Wi-Fi 7 and a PoE switch.
UniFi Express 7 is a super-compact gateway that can grow with mesh Wi-Fi. It runs only the Network app, so it suits simple sites, not ones wanting cameras and door control on the same box.
g: Power over Ethernet: power and data on one network cable.

quiz.q: A small shop wants a simple gateway plus Wi-Fi in one device. Which fits the product positioning best?
quiz.w: Dream Router 7 combines gateway, Wi-Fi 7 and a PoE switch. The others target larger sites.

quiz.q: What is limited about UniFi Express 7?
o: It only runs the Network app
quiz.w: Express runs only UniFi Network, so no Protect or Access on it.

quiz.q: Which tier is at the top of the gateway range?
quiz.w: Enterprise Firewall models are described as built for the most demanding networks.

quiz.q: What is PoE used for?
o: Sending power and data over one cable
quiz.w: PoE powers devices such as access points and cameras over the network cable.

pages.t: UniFi switches range from compact ones for tight spaces, through value and professional models, up to enterprise core switches. Higher tiers offer more PoE power, faster uplinks and routing. All are managed centrally without licence fees.
g: The fast port connecting a switch to the rest of the network.

pages.t: Access points include ceiling models, enterprise models for crowded places such as stadiums, in-wall units and weatherproof outdoor units. Names starting U7 are Wi-Fi 7 and U6 are Wi-Fi 6. Most are powered over PoE from a switch.
g: A device that gives Wi-Fi coverage and connects by cable to the network.

pages.t: APs can run standalone, but wireless mesh needs a UniFi console, and Ubiquiti recommends a UniFi gateway for the smoothest setup. The free Design Center helps plan coverage. Good habit: plan where APs go before quoting.
g: Access points linking to each other wirelessly instead of every one needing a cable.

quiz.q: A stadium needs Wi-Fi for very many users. Which AP category matches?
quiz.w: The Enterprise category is for critical, high-density sites, including arenas.

quiz.q: What do UniFi APs need if you want wireless mesh between them?
quiz.w: Ubiquiti says wireless meshing requires a UniFi console and is not available for standalone AP setups.
g: Access points linking to each other wirelessly.

quiz.q: Which tool helps plan AP coverage?
quiz.w: The free UniFi Design Center is for planning Wi-Fi coverage on a floor plan.

pages.t: UniFi Protect runs on a UniFi console and records to local storage. Cameras come in bullet, dome, turret, compact and PTZ styles. Motion, person and vehicle detection are built in. Ubiquiti states no licence fees.
g: Pan-tilt-zoom: a camera you can steer and zoom.
Network video recorder: the box that stores camera footage.

pages.t: UniFi Access controls doors with hubs and readers. People can open doors with cards, fobs or a phone. Starter kits exist for single doors, elevators and vehicle gates.
g: The box that connects to the lock and reader and enforces who may enter.

pages.t: Access and Protect work together, so door control and camera video can be handled in one UniFi system. Both are managed from the same platform. That is a strong angle for sites that already run UniFi networking.

quiz.q: Where does UniFi Protect record by default?
o: Local storage on the console or recorder
quiz.w: Protect records to local storage on your console. Cloud connection is optional, mainly for remote access.

quiz.q: A customer wants door control linked with video of who entered. What do you suggest?
quiz.w: Access and Protect work together, so door control and camera video sit in one system.

quiz.q: What connects the lock and reader in UniFi Access?
quiz.w: Readers connect to a hub, which handles access rights.

pages.t: UniFi Talk is a business VoIP phone system with touchscreen desk and wall phones. It can run on a UniFi console or work with a third-party PBX or SIP provider. Outbound calling needs a Talk service subscription or your own SIP provider.
g: Voice over IP: phone calls over the internet.
Private branch exchange: a company's internal phone system.

pages.t: UniFi Connect covers digital signage, lighting and EV charging on the UniFi platform. It is the add-on line, a possible fit for hotels and shops that want more than networking.
g: Screens showing menus, ads or info, managed centrally.

pages.t: Some UniFi gateways add mobile internet: Dream Router 5G Max has built-in 5G, and Cloud Gateway Industrial is a multi-WAN gateway with remote SIM support. Mobile links suit sites where fixed internet is slow to install or needs a backup line.
g: Mobile internet used when the main line fails, or as the main line where no cable exists.

quiz.q: Which UniFi app manages digital signage and EV charging?
quiz.w: Connect covers signage, lighting and EV charging.

quiz.q: A pop-up shop has no cable internet yet. Which is the most relevant UniFi product type?
o: A 5G-capable device such as Dream Router 5G Max
quiz.w: 5G devices use mobile internet as primary or backup connection.

quiz.q: What is a cost to remember when selling UniFi Talk?
o: Calling service (a subscription or your own SIP provider) is separate from the phones
quiz.w: Ubiquiti says it charges no extra licence fees, but outbound calling needs a Talk service subscription or your own SIP provider.

pages.t: A UniFi site is run by a console on site. Security rules are applied locally and Protect records locally. If the internet drops, the local network should keep running and recordings stay on the console.
g: Running on hardware at the customer's own location, not in someone else's data centre.

pages.t: For remote access Ubiquiti offers Site Manager (unifi.ui.com) and the mobile apps, described as free. One login can reach many sites, which suits resellers and MSPs looking after several customers.
g: Managed service provider: a company that runs IT for customers.

pages.t: Ubiquiti states no licence fees for the network apps and for Protect cameras, whether 4 or 4,000. It contrasts itself with vendors that charge per device or per year. Always confirm exceptions, such as Talk calling service.

quiz.q: Where does a UniFi site mainly handle traffic and recording?
quiz.w: The gateway runs on premises, with remote management added on top.

quiz.q: A reseller looks after ten small customers. Which feature helps most?
o: Site Manager for remote multi-site access
quiz.w: Site Manager and the apps give remote access to many sites.

quiz.q: How do you describe UniFi's licensing for Protect?
o: No licence fees stated by Ubiquiti
quiz.w: Ubiquiti says Protect licensing is $0, whatever the number of cameras.

quiz.q: What does 'on-premises' mean?
quiz.w: On-premises means the hardware sits at the customer's site.
g: Running at the customer's own location.

pages.t: Besides UniFi, Ubiquiti has lines built for internet providers: airMAX for point-to-multipoint and point-to-point radio links, airFiber for high-capacity point-to-point links, and UFiber for fibre (GPON) networks. They are aimed at carriers, not offices.
g: Wireless Internet Service Provider: sells internet to homes or firms using radio links.
A radio link joining exactly two places, for example two buildings.

pages.t: These ISP products are managed in UISP, a separate system from UniFi. Typical customers are WISPs and installers building links between sites. It is a different conversation from an office Wi-Fi quote.
g: One radio mast serving many customer antennas.

pages.t: If the customer talks about subscribers, towers or linking far-apart buildings, think airMAX or UISP. If they talk about offices, hotels or shops, think UniFi. Check models carefully: lines are not interchangeable.

quiz.q: A customer sells internet to farms using radio masts. Which Ubiquiti area fits?
quiz.w: airMAX radios and the UISP management system are aimed at wireless ISPs.

quiz.q: Which line is aimed at fibre ISPs?
quiz.w: UFiber is Ubiquiti's fibre (GPON) line, managed in UISP. UniFi Access is door control and EdgeMax is wired routing.

quiz.q: What is a WISP?
quiz.w: A WISP sells internet over radio links.

lessons.title: Choosing the line for a customer

pages.t: Ask what the customer needs to do: connect, cover with Wi-Fi, watch, lock or call. Then pick the app. Same console, more apps. The quote usually starts with gateway, switch, APs, then grows.

Common buyers: SMB offices and shops want gateway, PoE switch, APs, a few cameras. Hospitality often needs many APs, guest Wi-Fi, door access, phones. Prosumers may want a Dream Router and cameras. ISPs: airMAX, UISP, fibre.

How many sites? How many people on Wi-Fi? Cameras or doors too? Is internet cabled or mobile only? Who will manage it afterwards? The answers decide model size, PoE budget and whether remote management matters.

quiz.q: A 20-room hotel wants guest Wi-Fi in every room corridor and door control. What do you start with?
o: Gateway, PoE switch, APs and Access
quiz.w: A hotel needs network, many APs and door access, which UniFi can cover in one system.

quiz.q: A small shop with four cameras and simple Wi-Fi. Best match?
o: Cloud Gateway with Protect and a PoE switch plus an AP
quiz.w: A small-site gateway running Protect, plus PoE gear, covers it.

quiz.q: A WISP wants links between two towers. Which area?
quiz.w: Point-to-point links are the airMAX and airFiber territory.

quiz.q: Which question helps size the PoE budget?
o: How many APs and cameras need power?
What colour should the devices be?
quiz.w: PoE devices such as APs and cameras draw from the switch's power budget.
g: Total power a switch can supply to connected devices.

pages.t: One system for network, cameras, doors and phones; no licence fees on management; easy rollout for installers; a wide range from small to large. For SMB and hospitality, that unified story is a strong selling point.
g: Everything managed in one place instead of separate tools per product.

pages.t: UniFi is a single-vendor ecosystem: its strongest features usually need UniFi devices together. Big regulated organisations may have specific certification, support or compliance demands, so check their requirements before you promise.

UniFi targets home, prosumer and business users, and Ubiquiti has faced public security criticism in the past. Do not claim it replaces every enterprise platform. Present it as a strong fit for SMB, and let the customer's needs decide.
g: A vendor aimed at large organisations, typically with deep support contracts and compliance features.

quiz.q: What is UniFi's biggest sales strength for an SMB?
o: Only works with other vendors' gear
One system for network, cameras, doors and phones
quiz.w: The unified story across areas is the main strength.

quiz.q: A large bank asks if UniFi meets its compliance rules. Best answer?
o: Check their specific requirements before promising
quiz.w: Regulated organisations have specific demands, so verify rather than assume.

quiz.q: What does 'single-vendor ecosystem' mean?
o: The best features need the vendor's own devices together
The vendor sells only one product
Customers can use only one site
quiz.w: UniFi's apps and devices work best when used together.

pages.t: Point to the range: Enterprise Firewall gateways, enterprise switches and enterprise Wi-Fi exist, alongside small sites. Add that the choice depends on size and requirements, and offer to involve a colleague for bigger projects.
The console runs on site and recording is local. Remote access via Site Manager is optional. A sound answer: the site runs locally, the cloud portal adds remote convenience.
g: Being tied to a vendor because switching away is hard or costly.

pages.t: Management and Protect carry no licence fees per Ubiquiti. Talk phone service and some extras are separate subscriptions. Never quote prices from memory: send resellers to current price lists and your sales contact.

quiz.q: A customer fears the cloud is mandatory. What is a good reply?
o: Everything runs only in the cloud
The console runs on site; remote access is optional
Cameras stream live to Ubiquiti servers
quiz.w: The gateway runs on premises, with remote portals on top.

quiz.q: 'Is there a yearly fee per camera?' What do you say?
o: Ubiquiti states no licence fees for Protect
quiz.w: Ubiquiti says licensing is $0 whether 4 or 4,000 cameras.

quiz.q: Which cost is separate from hardware?
quiz.w: Talk hardware and service subscriptions are separate costs.

quiz.q: What should you avoid in a customer chat?
quiz.w: Prices change; use current price lists instead.

pages.t: Every UniFi project is a mix of gateway, switches, APs plus optional apps: Protect, Access, Talk, Connect. ISP projects are another family: airMAX, airFiber, UFiber with UISP.
A reseller with many small customers values multi-site remote management through Site Manager. A single big site values Enterprise or Pro-level gateways and switches with more PoE and faster uplinks.

Very large, regulated or unusual projects need a colleague or the vendor. Your job: spot the customer type, ask the right questions, and name the right product family. Detail comes from the specialists.

quiz.q: An MSP manages 30 small clients and wants a single view. What feature is most relevant?
quiz.w: Site Manager gives remote access to many sites.

quiz.q: A farm co-op wants to share one internet line to a barn 2 km away. Best direction?
quiz.w: Linking distant buildings is point-to-point wireless territory.

quiz.q: A cafe wants Wi-Fi, two cameras and a menu screen on one console. Which apps?
quiz.w: Network handles Wi-Fi, Protect cameras, Connect signage.

quiz.q: A government agency with strict rules asks about UniFi. What do you do?
o: Collect their requirements and involve a colleague
quiz.w: Regulated cases need verified answers, so escalate.
